_about: The one central recording sheet (Zafar, 14 Nov): every question for Mum, and everything still to record, one row each. Grammar first, then each game (sections, in order). Only ever added to: a row is never deleted or renumbered; an answered row stays, marked. Kutchi only where Mum (or the family) said it, with who said it; never a guess. Statuses: to record (no Kutchi: needs Mum's Kutchi; Kutchi: just record), to confirm, answered, recorded (date and clip ids from data/family-audio.json), confirmed (spelling), closed (the game no longer needs it). keys tie a row to the language engine's needs (build/tools/ops/recordings.mjs adds and moves them). Made into docs/language/recording-sheet.docx and .md by build/tools/lang/recording-sheet.mjs. Imported 14 Nov from every earlier sheet (build/reports/s20-recording-sheet.md lists them).

rows.en: Which dishes are really ours?: These are the dishes we'd like in the game, a mix of Kutch cooking and the East African food we grew up with. For each: do you really make it, what's it called at home, and what would you add, remove or change? Which are more Kenya or Tanzania, and which are more Kutch? And what's missing that you'd expect in your kitchen? Chai · maani / rotli · daal · chaat bowl (chana bateta) · samosa · mishkaki with chips · chips mayai · mogo · makai (corn on the cob) · mandazi · dahi puri / sev puri · dabeli · falooda · jalebi · sheer khurma · biryani / pilau For the ones you really make, name five to ten things that go in each, and say if it belongs to an occasion (Eid morning, everyday dinner, guests, a rainy day).
rows.for: Kitchen talk (about 20–30 minutes, relaxed)
rows.source: Round 4 I36; Round 3 I36; Combined I36

rows.en: How you make the first six: For each, talk through what goes in and in what order, what you do at each step, and how you know it's ready. This becomes the recipe in the game. 1. Chai: water, tea, boil, milk, sugar? Masala, elchi, ginger? When do they go in? 2. Maani / rotli: flour, water, oil or ghee? How thin? When do you flip it? Ghee on top? 3. Daal: which daal? What goes in the tadka and in what order (jeeru, rai, hing, garlic, chilli…)? Onion, tomato? 4. Chaat bowl: every topping, in the usual order. 5. Samosa: which filling? How do you fold it? 6. Mishkaki: which meat, what else goes on the skewer, the marinade, the chips on the side with chilli and lemon?
rows.for: Kitchen talk (about 20–30 minutes, relaxed)
rows.source: Round 4 I37; Round 3 I37; Combined I37

rows.en: Who likes what: In the game everyone has their own taste and the child has to listen. Tell us the real ones, silly ones included: who takes three sugars, who has no milk, who won't touch chilli, who always wants extra onion, who hates what.
rows.for: Kitchen talk (about 20–30 minutes, relaxed)
rows.source: Round 4 I38; Round 3 I38; Combined I38

rows.en: A real chai order, in one breath: Finally, say two or three complete orders the way they'd be said at home: "chai with two sugars, no milk, half a cup", "two maani and daal, no onion", "one veg skewer and one mixed, with chips". These are the sentences the game will copy.
